pll2d1c6-d1e3514.summary: Asks why the soul was united to a body, since it would seem more dignified without one.

pll2d1c6-d1e3517.summary: First answer: because God willed it, and the cause of his will is not to be sought.
claims: God's will is the cause, and its cause is not sought.

pll2d1c6-d1e3520.summary: Second answer: God united soul and body to show in human nature an example of the blessed union between God and spirit, loved with the whole heart and seen face to face. The creature might think it could not be so closely united to its Creator, unless it saw spirit united to lowly flesh in such love that it does not wish to leave it (2 Cor 5:4).
claims: The union of soul and body exemplifies union with God.
Spirit does not wish to be stripped of its body.

pll2d1c6-d1e3547.summary: Continues: as an example of the future society of God and rational spirit, God joined the soul to body, so that if God could join such unequal natures in friendship, he could raise the lowly rational creature to share his glory. Lest the spirit seem too lowered, providence added that it would later be raised with its glorified body to the angels' company. God placed angels in heaven and souls with bodies on earth, giving both a rule of obedience, and made man of body from earth and soul from nothing; souls are also joined to bodies to merit a greater crown.
claims: God made man of a body from earth and a soul from nothing.
Angels and humans were given a rule of obedience.
The soul with its glorified body will be raised to the angels.

pll2d1c6-d1e3561.summary: Concludes that rational creation is divided into angelic, wholly spiritual, and human, partly spiritual and partly corporeal.
claims: Rational creatures are angelic and human.

pll2d1c6-d1e3564.summary: Announces the order: first rational spiritual creatures, angels, so that reason moves from contemplating the Creator to the worthier creature, then corporeal creatures, rational and non-rational, so that the mystery of the uncreated Trinity is followed by the teaching on tripartite creation.
claims: Angels will be treated first, then corporeal creatures.

pl-l2d1c6.summary: Asks why the soul was united to a body when it would seem more dignified without one. First, because God willed it, and his will's cause is not sought. Second, to show in human nature an example of the blessed union between God and spirit: if spirit can be united in such love to lowly flesh that it does not wish to leave it (2 Cor 5:4), God can raise the rational creature to share his glory. Lest the spirit seem too lowered, providence ordained that with its glorified body it be raised to the company of the angels, receiving by grace what it lacked by creation. God set the angels in heaven and humans on earth, giving both a rule of obedience, and made man of two substances, body from earth and soul from nothing; souls are joined to bodies also to merit a greater crown. Rational creation is thus angelic and human. The treatise will treat first angels, then corporeal creatures, rational and non-rational, following the Trinity with the tripartite creation.
claims: The soul was united to the body because God willed it.
The union of soul and body is an example of the future union of God and the rational spirit.
Spirit loves its body so that it does not wish to leave it.
The glorified soul with its body will be raised to the angels' company.
God gave both angels and humans a rule of obedience.
Man is made of a body from earth and a soul from nothing.
The treatise will consider angels first, then corporeal creatures.
